---
title: "Verifying a bench"
description: "arduino-io info and a short stream test"
toc: true
---

Run through this once for every newly built bench, and again any time you
suspect the board, the host setup or the firmware. The example output below
is from a **Portenta H7** — expect different numbers on other boards, but the
same shape of output.

## 1. The board is found

```bash
arduino-io list
```

The board should appear in the main list. If it instead appears in a "Not
probed" block, that is a permissions problem — see [Linux
host](host-linux.qmd) or [Windows host](host-windows.qmd) — or another
process already has it open.

## 2. `arduino-io info`

```bash
$ arduino-io info
board:            Portenta H7 (id 0x0201)
protocol version: 0x0001
pins:             26 (analog: 7)
resolution:       adc 16 bits, pwm 12 bits, dac 12 bits
voltages:         vref 3300 mV, io 3300 mV
flags:            0x000F vendor-interface pulldown streaming events
queue depth:      32
stream channels:  up to 8
stream period:    1 us or longer (up to 1000000 Hz, bounded by the sketch's loop() rate)
event pins:       up to 8
transport:        device recipient, interface 0 (claimed)
```

Read the **`flags`** line first: it is the quickest way to confirm *which*
firmware is actually on the board. `streaming` and `events` appear only if
the sketch was built from a `UsbIo` revision that has them — a board that
answers `info` but is missing `streaming` either cannot stream at all (the
two Renesas boards, UNO R4 Minima and Nano R4) or is running older firmware;
see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd) to tell the two apart.

## 3. `arduino-io caps`

```bash
$ arduino-io caps
PIN  CAPS  NOTES
0    D-P-
...
15   -A--  analog #0 (analog-only pad)
...
21   DA-C  analog #6, DAC
D digital I/O, A analog input, P PWM, C DAC
```

Confirms the pin capability table matches what [Supported
boards](boards.qmd) documents for this board — in particular, which pin
number is A0 on *this* board.

## 4. Digital write

```bash
arduino-io mode 13 output && arduino-io write 13 1
```

should turn on an LED on pin 13 (or the equivalent on your board — check
`caps`); `write 13 0` turns it off.

## 5. Analog read

```bash
arduino-io mode 15 analog && arduino-io aread 15 --volts
```

(use A0's actual pin number for your board) should read a plausible voltage —
0 V or the reference voltage on a floating pin, or a known voltage if you
have wired a reference into it.

## 6. Stream test {#stream-summary-fields}

On a board that reports `streaming` in its `flags`:

```bash
arduino-io mode 15 analog && arduino-io mode 16 analog
arduino-io stream 15,16 --hz 1000 --seconds 3 --volts --csv samples.csv
```

```
stream: 3029 records (6058 samples) in 3.028 s (1000.4 Hz achieved per channel);
device overruns 0, seq gaps 0, host drops 0, resyncs 0, stale records 0
```

Each field means:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `device overruns` | the board's own ring buffer overflowed because it could not send records fast enough |
| `seq gaps` | records lost before reaching the host, detected as a gap in the device's per-record sequence number (includes device overruns) |
| `host drops` | decoded records the host had to discard because the consumer was not reading fast enough (the queue filled) |
| `resyncs` | times the driver lost synchronization on the stream's framing marker and had to resynchronize |
| `stale records` | records sampled before *this* session's start, left over in the endpoint by an earlier session, and discarded |

**All zeros is the AMLab acceptance criterion**: it means every sample
requested was recorded, in order, with no loss anywhere in the chain. A
recording with any nonzero field is not a complete recording — investigate
before trusting the data (see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd) for
overruns specifically).

## Checklist

- [ ] `arduino-io list` shows the board (not in "Not probed")
- [ ] `arduino-io info` reports the expected board name and pin counts
- [ ] the `flags` line shows the firmware capabilities the experiment needs
- [ ] `arduino-io caps` matches the board's documented pin table
- [ ] a digital write toggles a visible LED
- [ ] an analog read returns a plausible voltage
- [ ] (streaming boards only) a stream test's summary line is all zeros at
      the rate the experiment needs

A bench that passes every item is ready for an experiment.
